To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dietary fat and carbohydrates, and alcohol are the most important dietary factors affecting postprandial lipid metabolism.

weight loss is associated with reduced PPL; the type of dietary fat, the amount of carbohydrates, and the protein content are important factors that affect PPL; the effect of polyphenols and other bioactive components on PPL is controversial; and the effect of alcohol on PPL is dose dependent.
dietary fat quantity and quality, carbohydrates and alcohol intake, as well as weight loss and dietary patterns, have an important impact on PPL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dietary components on postprandial lipidemia.
the impact of diet on PPL, which is considered a cardiovascular risk factor.
the impact of diet on PPL in healthy subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of diet on postprandial lipid metabolism is complex and multifactorial, and it depends on the type of dietary component and the amount and quality of the diet.
there are no clear dietary recommendations for the modulation of PPL.
the dietary components and dietary patterns have a significant impact on PPL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary fat, carbohydrate, and protein quantity and quality, alcohol, polyphenols, as well as dietary patterns have an impact on PPL in a dose- and time-dependent manner.
dietary interventions, particularly those based on weight loss and the replacement of saturated fat with unsaturated fat, can improve PPL in humans.
a high-fat, low-carbohydrate, low-glycemic load diet, with a low glycemic index and high fiber content, and a high intake of monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFAs) is recommended to reduce PPL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dietary interventions are effective in reducing PPL.

the dietary impact on PPL is multifactorial and depends not only on the amount of each macronutrient but also on its composition, as well as the interactions with other dietary components and lifestyle factors.

a diet rich in unsaturated fatty acids and polyphenols, with a moderate carbohydrate intake, is associated with lower PPL, whereas diets high in trans fatty acids, saturated fatty acids, refined carbohydrates and/or alcohol have the opposite effect.
